name: Question 1
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x+3xy,\,y(-2)=-1
$$

The **implicit** Euler method is applied with step size $Δx=\frac{1}{3}.$ 
Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and the current value $y.$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(2{x}_{\text{new}}+3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}_{\text{new}}+{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{2}{3}{x}_{\text{new}}+{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{2}{3}{x}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(1-{x}_{\text{new}}) & =y+\frac{2}{3}{x}_{\text{new}} \\ 3{y}_{\text{new}}(1-{x}_{\text{new}}) & =3y+2{x}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(3-3{x}_{\text{new}}) & =3y+2{x}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{3y+2{x}_{\text{new}}}{3-3{x}_{\text{new}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=2x+3xy,y(−2)=−1 The implicit Euler method is applied with step size Δx=13. Find the general formula for the new y value, ynew, in terms of the new value xnew and the current value y.

a
ynew=y+23xnew+xnewy
b
ynew=3y+2xnew3+3xnew
c
ynew=y+23xnew−y
d
ynew=3y+2xnew3−3y
e
ynew=3y+2xnew3−3xnew
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y0=y(x0), the implicit Euler method with step size Δx is given by Δy=ynew′⋅Δx, with ynew′=f(xnew,ynew) evaluated at the next x and y values.

In general, Δy is given by

Δy=ynew′⋅Δx=(2xnew+3xnewynew)⋅13=23xnew+xnewynew

We substitute this into ynew=y+Δy and solve for the general formula for ynew:

ynew=y+Δyynew=y+23xnew+xnewynewynew−xnewynew=y+23xnewynew(1−xnew)=y+23xnew3ynew(1−xnew)=3y+2xnewynew(3−3xnew)=3y+2xnewynew=3y+2xnew3−3xnew
